Definition: probably from G939 (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively):--king.
BiblicalUsage: Basileus is a king, and the word follows Jesus from His birth to His cross to His return. The wise men ask where He is who is born King of the Jews, Jesus tells Pilate He was born to be a King and to bear witness to the truth, Pilate writes King of the Jews on the cross, and John sees Him coming with King of kings and Lord of lords written on His vesture and His thigh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title King follows Jesus because it is true at every point of His life, and the men who used it as a charge against Him were telling the truth without knowing it. Pilate wrote it in mockery, the wise men spoke it in worship, and I hold that one day every knee will confess what the cross already declared.
